union.summary: Cross-sheet unbounded refs (`Sheet2!A:A`) are deliberately left unexpanded, but they now lex as REFERENCE and reach `toSrefs()`, which throws `Invalid Reference` — breaking `buildDependantsMap` and therefore every subsequent edit/recalc on the whole sheet (docs claim they merely evaluate to `#ERROR!`).
union.evidence: `toSrefs` cross-sheet branch: coordinates.ts:238-243 calls `parseRange(localRef)` → `parseRef('A')` → throw (parseRef: coordinates.ts:336-338). Reached with an unexpanded `SHEET2!A:A` from: packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts:333 (`toSrefs(extractReferences(expandUnboundedRanges(...)))` — the `isCrossSheetRef(r) continue` guard is *inside* the loop body, after the generator has already thrown), packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:574,585,601, packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2615 (`fetchGridByReferences`) and sheet.ts:2712 (`buildGlobalDependantsMap`). `buildDependantsMap` scans *all* formula cells (memory.ts:323-333), so one cell containing `=Sheet2!A:A` makes `setData`/`removeData` (sheet.ts:1063, 1144) reject for the entire sheet. Fix belongs either in `toSrefs`/the new expansion (skip or reject unbounded refs defensively) or by rejecting the token at commit time.

union.summary: All four formula-rewriting functions (`shiftFormula`, `moveFormula`, `relocateFormula`, `redirectFormula`) call `parseARef` on each `:`-separated endpoint and throw on a column-only/row-only endpoint, so insert/delete row-column, move row-column, copy-paste and cut-paste all throw on any sheet containing `=SUM(A:A)` / `=SUM(1:1)` / `=AVERAGE(B2:B)`.
union.evidence: shifting.ts:373-374 (`shiftFormula`), :80-81 (`moveFormula`), :184-185 (`relocateFormula`), :242-243 (`redirectFormula`) — `parseARef` requires `^(\$?)([A-Za-z]+)(\$?)(\d+)$` (coordinates.ts:366-369) and throws for `A` or `1`. Previously `A:A` never produced a REFERENCE token so these branches were unreachable. Reachable call chains: sheet.ts:1166-1192 insertRows/deleteRows/insertColumns/deleteColumns → memory.ts:181 `shiftGrid` → shifting.ts:456; memory.ts:233 `moveGrid` → shifting.ts:120; clipboard.ts:25 and :151 (`relocateGrid`, autofill); sheet.ts:2375 (`redirectFormulasForCut`). None wrap the call in try/catch.

union.summary: In the collaborative store the same `shiftFormula`/`moveFormula` throw happens *in the middle* of a Yorkie document mutation, after rows/columns have already been inserted or deleted but before dimensions, styles, merges, charts and threads are shifted — leaving the shared document in a partially-shifted state.
union.evidence: yorkie-worksheet-structure.ts:283-290: `insertYorkieWorksheetAxis` / `deleteYorkieWorksheetAxis` already mutated `ws`, then `rewriteFormulaCells(ws, normalizeCell, (f) => shiftFormula(f, axis, index, count))` throws for a cell holding `=SUM(A:A)`; lines 292-343 (dimension/style/merge/anchor/thread shifting) never run. Same shape at :358-360 for `moveFormula`. Confirm by inserting a row on a doc whose cell contains `=SUM(A:A)`.

union.summary: The F4 absolute-reference toggle now fires on whole-column/whole-row REFERENCE tokens and produces a corrupt reference (`A:A` → `$$A:A`, `1:1` → `$$1:1`), silently invalidating the user's formula.
union.evidence: worksheet.ts:1261 `findReferenceTokenAtCursor` now returns `A:A`; the digit scan at :1270-1278 finds no digits before `:` so `colPart=''` and `rowPart='A:A'`, and :1291 builds `'$' + '' + '$' + 'A:A'` = `$$A:A`, written back at :1303-1307. Previously `A:A` was never a REFERENCE token so this path was unreachable.

union.summary: Expanded whole-column/row ranges are materialised cell-by-cell by untouched code: `buildDependantsMap` creates a dependants entry for every cell in the expanded range on *every* edit, and `fetchGridByReferences` awaits one `store.get()` per cell — O(rows×cols) work/memory that can hang or OOM the editor on a realistically tall sheet.
union.evidence: sheet.ts:2615-2629 loops `for (const sref of toSrefs(references))` with an `await this.store.get(anchor)` per cell; memory.ts:333 and yorkie-store.ts:574/585/601 do `toSrefs(...)` over the expanded range for every formula cell on every edit. With data at row 100000 (bounds max), `=SUM(A:A)` expands to `A1:A100000`. Neither path existed for unbounded refs before; nothing caps the expansion size.

union.summary: `CellIndex.bounds()` is documented and used as the extent of "populated cells", but the index also contains style-only (empty-value) cells, so a single formatted cell far down the sheet inflates every `A:A`/`1:1` expansion — and hence the dependants map and grid fetch — far beyond the real data extent.
union.evidence: memory.ts:97-100 `set()` indexes every cell it stores, including style-only cells; `findEdge` (memory.ts:163-178) has to filter them out explicitly with `(!!cell.v || !!cell.f)`, proving the index is not value-only. `bounds()` (cell-index.ts:128-149) applies no such filter, yet its doc comment and store.ts:75-79 both say "populated cells".

union.summary: The blank-skipping change in the shared `Arguments.iterate` silently changes results of existing *bounded*-range formulas across ~25 functions; MIN/MAX were adjusted for it but the logical and other statistical consumers were not.
union.evidence: arguments.ts:110-125 now skips blank cells for any range. Consumers not reconsidered: functions-logical.ts:111 (`AND`), :133 (`OR`), :174 (`XOR`) — `ref2bool` mapped a blank to `false` (arguments.ts:194), so `=AND(A1:A3)` with a blank A2 flips from FALSE to TRUE, and an all-blank range now returns TRUE instead of FALSE; functions-statistical.ts:31-41 (`AVERAGE`) and :56-65 (`MEDIAN`) return `ErrNode.VALUE` when nothing is yielded, so an all-blank bounded range now yields `#VALUE!` where it previously produced a number. Contrast functions-statistical.ts:95-98 and :120-123, where MIN/MAX *were* given explicit fallbacks for the new behaviour.

union.summary: The dependants map and the evaluation use two different snapshots of `getUsedBounds()`, so within a single recalculation pass the dependency graph and the expanded formula can disagree — a cell can be evaluated over a wider/narrower range than the one it is registered as depending on, leaving stale values.
union.evidence: memory.ts:329 computes `bounds` once when the map is built; calculator.ts:90-93 re-reads `await sheet.getUsedBounds()` per cell *after* `calculate` has already written cells (spill ghosts at calculator.ts:130+, `sheet.setCell`), which mutates the cell index and therefore the bounds mid-pass. To confirm: a spill/ghost write that extends the used bounds during a pass, followed by a whole-column formula later in topological order.

union.summary: `getUsedBounds()` is added as a required member of the exported `Store` interface, a breaking change for any implementer outside this repo (the package exports `Store`); all three in-repo implementations were updated, so nothing local breaks.
union.evidence: store.ts:75-79 adds the required method; in-repo implementers updated at memory.ts:315, readonly.ts:157, yorkie-store.ts:614. Making it optional (or providing a default) would keep external implementations compiling.

union.summary: Documentation describes contracts that no longer match the code: it claims whole-column highlighting is skipped and that cross-sheet unbounded refs evaluate to `#ERROR!`.
union.evidence: The doc's Limitations paragraph says `extractFormulaRanges` "skips unbounded refs", but formula.ts:396-420 now takes a `bounds` argument and resolves them (called with bounds at view/worksheet.ts:1131). It also says `Sheet2!A:A` evaluates to `#ERROR!`, whereas in practice `toSrefs` throws before evaluation (coordinates.ts:240 via memory.ts:333).

union.summary: Because the used bounds include the formula cell's own row/column, a whole-row/column ref can expand to a range containing the formula itself, turning a previously-impossible formula into a self-dependency that the untouched cycle detector marks `#REF!`.
union.evidence: expandUnboundedRanges resolves `1:1` against bounds that include the formula cell's column (index updated on write, memory.ts:99), so `=SUM(1:1)` written in `D1` expands to `A1:D1` and `calculate`'s `cycled` branch (calculator.ts:54-68) writes `#REF!`. Note the new tests deliberately place `=SUM(1:1)` at r2c4 (test/sheet/calculation.test.ts) so this case is never exercised.

union.summary: `shiftFormula` throws on the new whole-column/row tokens — inserting or deleting a row/column while any cell holds `=SUM(A:A)` aborts the structural edit mid-transaction
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/shifting.ts:372-374 splits a range REFERENCE token and calls `parseARef(startStr)`/`parseARef(endStr)`. `parseARef` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:366) matches `/^(\$?)([A-Za-z]+)(\$?)(\d+)$/` and throws `Invalid Reference` for the endpoint `A` (or `1`). Before this diff `A:A` never lexed as a REFERENCE token so it passed through untouched; now it does (packages/sheets/test/formula/formula.test.ts:4356 proves the lexer emits `A:A`). Reachable from MemStore.shift → shiftGrid → shiftFormula (packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts:181, packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/shifting.ts:456) and from the collaborative path packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-structure.ts:288-290, where the throw happens *after* `insertYorkieWorksheetAxis`/`deleteYorkieWorksheetAxis` have already mutated the Yorkie document (lines 282-286) — a half-applied structural change. No shifting test uses an unbounded ref (grep `A:A` under packages/sheets/test returns only formula/calculation tests). Fix belongs in shifting.ts (handle partial endpoints), not in the diff's new code.

union.summary: `relocateFormula` throws on whole-column/row tokens — copy-paste and autofill of a cell containing `=SUM(A:A)` fail
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/shifting.ts:183-185 calls `parseARef(startStr.toUpperCase())` on each half of a range token, which throws for the endpoint `A`/`1` (coordinates.ts:366-369). Called by `relocateGrid` for paste (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/clipboard.ts:25) and by `cloneCellForAutofill` for drag-fill (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/clipboard.ts:151). Neither call site is guarded by try/catch, so copying a cell whose formula uses the newly-legal `A:A` syntax throws instead of pasting.

union.summary: `redirectFormula` throws on whole-column/row tokens — one `=SUM(A:A)` anywhere in the sheet breaks every cut-paste
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/shifting.ts:241-243 `parseARef(startStr)` on each range endpoint throws for `A`/`1`. `redirectFormulasForCut` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2366-2375) walks the *entire* formula grid and calls `redirectFormula(cell.f, refMap)` on every formula cell, so a single unbounded reference anywhere in the sheet makes all subsequent cut-paste operations throw (invoked at sheet.ts:2191 and sheet.ts:2321).

union.summary: `moveFormula` throws on whole-column/row tokens — moving rows/columns breaks when a formula uses `A:A`
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/shifting.ts:79-84 calls `parseARef` on both halves of a range REFERENCE token; throws for `A`/`1`. Reached via `moveGrid` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/shifting.ts:120) and via the Yorkie move path packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-structure.ts:358-360, again after `moveYorkieWorksheetAxis` has already mutated the document (line 356).

union.summary: Cross-sheet dependency walker still feeds raw `extractReferences()` output into `toSrefs`, which throws on `A:A` — cross-sheet recalculation aborts
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2711-2712 (`toSrefs(extractReferences(cell.f))`) and sheet.ts:2736-2738 were not updated with `expandUnboundedRanges`. `toSrefs` → `parseRange('A:A')` → `parseRef('A')` throws `Invalid Reference` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:250-252, 336-338). Step 1 is hit when a sheet has a formula containing both a cross-sheet ref and a whole-column ref (e.g. `=SUM(A:A)+Sheet2!A1`); step 2 (line 2738) iterates *all* formulas of every referenced remote sheet, so any `A:A` in a remote sheet breaks the walk regardless of the local formula. `recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (sheet.ts:2773-2811) has only try/finally, no catch, so the error propagates out and cross-sheet values go stale.

union.summary: The blank-skip in `Arguments.iterate` is not limited to unbounded ranges, silently changing results of existing bounded-range formulas across ~15 functions
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/formula/arguments.ts:116-123 skips blank cells for *every* range argument, not just expanded unbounded ones. Consumers never touched by the diff change behaviour: `averageFunc` now returns `#VALUE!` for an all-blank range because `count===0` (packages/sheets/src/formula/functions-statistical.ts:31,39-41) where it previously averaged zeros; `medianFunc` likewise (functions-statistical.ts:56,63-65); `productFunc` previously returned 0 when any cell in the range was blank and now ignores it (packages/sheets/src/formula/functions-math.ts:247); denominators change for `stdevFunc`/`stdevpFunc`/`varFunc`/`varpFunc` (functions-statistical.ts:645,670,695,720) and for `geomeanFunc`/`harmeanFunc`/`avedevFunc`/`devsqFunc`/`modeFunc` (functions-statistical.ts:1242,1261,1280,1299,745); `gcdFunc`/`lcmFunc` also change (functions-math.ts:874,898). Existing user formulas over ordinary ranges like `=AVERAGE(A1:A10)` produce different values after this change.

union.summary: `AND`/`OR`/`XOR` over a range silently flip results: blank cells used to evaluate to FALSE and are now skipped entirely
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/formula/functions-logical.ts:111 (`andFunc`), :133 (`orFunc`), :174 (`xorFunc`) iterate via `BoolArgs.iterate`, which now drops blank cells (packages/sheets/src/formula/arguments.ts:116-123). Previously `ref2bool` mapped a blank cell to `false` (arguments.ts:190-196), so `=AND(A1:A3)` with a blank A2 returned FALSE; it now returns TRUE when the other two are true. Existing spreadsheets relying on the old semantics change value with no migration or test covering the difference.

union.summary: Formula-range highlighting resolves unbounded refs against `dimensionRange` while evaluation clamps to used bounds, so the highlight and the computed range disagree
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:1131 calls `extractFormulaRanges(text, this.sheet?.dimensionRange)`, and `extractFormulaRanges` resolves unbounded refs with those bounds (packages/sheets/src/formula/formula.ts:414-417), whereas the calculator expands the same reference against `sheet.getUsedBounds()` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts:90-92, sheet.ts:2604-2606). `=SUM(A:A)` therefore highlights a different extent than the cells actually summed.

union.summary: `getUsedBounds` is a new *required* member of the publicly exported `Store` interface — a breaking change for any out-of-repo implementer
union.evidence: packages/sheets/src/store/store.ts:80 adds `getUsedBounds(): Promise<Range | undefined>` with no default, and `Store` is re-exported from the package entry point (packages/sheets/src/index.ts:351). All three in-repo implementations were updated (memory.ts:315, readonly.ts:157, packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:614), so the breakage is only for external implementers; making it optional (with an `undefined` fallback in Sheet.getUsedBounds) would avoid it.

union.summary: A whole-column total placed in the same column now self-references, because the used bounds include the formula cell itself
union.evidence: `CellIndex.bounds()` (packages/sheets/src/store/cell-index.ts:128-149) counts the formula cell, so `=SUM(A:A)` written in A100 expands to `A1:A100` and `MemStore.buildDependantsMap` (packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts:333) records A100 as a dependant of itself, feeding a self-edge into `calculate`'s cycle handling (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts). I could not confirm how `calculate` reacts to a self-edge (graceful `#REF!` vs. hang); a column-total in its own column is a common layout, and no test covers it.

Reached via `moveGrid` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/shifting.ts:120) and via the Yorkie move path packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-structure.ts:358-360, again after `moveYorkieWorksheetAxis` has already mutated the document (line 356).

per_sample.summary: Cross-sheet dependency walker still feeds raw `extractReferences()` output into `toSrefs`, which throws on `A:A` — cross-sheet recalculation aborts
per_sample.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2711-2712 (`toSrefs(extractReferences(cell.f))`) and sheet.ts:2736-2738 were not updated with `expandUnboundedRanges`. `toSrefs` → `parseRange('A:A')` → `parseRef('A')` throws `Invalid Reference` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:250-252, 336-338). Step 1 is hit when a sheet has a formula containing both a cross-sheet ref and a whole-column ref (e.g. `=SUM(A:A)+Sheet2!A1`); step 2 (line 2738) iterates *all* formulas of every referenced remote sheet, so any `A:A` in a remote sheet breaks the walk regardless of the local formula. `recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (sheet.ts:2773-2811) has only try/finally, no catch, so the error propagates out and cross-sheet values go stale.

per_sample.summary: The blank-skip in `Arguments.iterate` is not limited to unbounded ranges, silently changing results of existing bounded-range formulas across ~15 functions
per_sample.evidence: packages/sheets/src/formula/arguments.ts:116-123 skips blank cells for *every* range argument, not just expanded unbounded ones. Consumers never touched by the diff change behaviour: `averageFunc` now returns `#VALUE!` for an all-blank range because `count===0` (packages/sheets/src/formula/functions-statistical.ts:31,39-41) where it previously averaged zeros; `medianFunc` likewise (functions-statistical.ts:56,63-65); `productFunc` previously returned 0 when any cell in the range was blank and now ignores it (packages/sheets/src/formula/functions-math.ts:247); denominators change for `stdevFunc`/`stdevpFunc`/`varFunc`/`varpFunc` (functions-statistical.ts:645,670,695,720) and for `geomeanFunc`/`harmeanFunc`/`avedevFunc`/`devsqFunc`/`modeFunc` (functions-statistical.ts:1242,1261,1280,1299,745); `gcdFunc`/`lcmFunc` also change (functions-math.ts:874,898). Existing user formulas over ordinary ranges like `=AVERAGE(A1:A10)` produce different values after this change.

per_sample.summary: `AND`/`OR`/`XOR` over a range silently flip results: blank cells used to evaluate to FALSE and are now skipped entirely
per_sample.evidence: packages/sheets/src/formula/functions-logical.ts:111 (`andFunc`), :133 (`orFunc`), :174 (`xorFunc`) iterate via `BoolArgs.iterate`, which now drops blank cells (packages/sheets/src/formula/arguments.ts:116-123). Previously `ref2bool` mapped a blank cell to `false` (arguments.ts:190-196), so `=AND(A1:A3)` with a blank A2 returned FALSE; it now returns TRUE when the other two are true. Existing spreadsheets relying on the old semantics change value with no migration or test covering the difference.

per_sample.summary: Formula-range highlighting resolves unbounded refs against `dimensionRange` while evaluation clamps to used bounds, so the highlight and the computed range disagree
per_sample.evidence: packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:1131 calls `extractFormulaRanges(text, this.sheet?.dimensionRange)`, and `extractFormulaRanges` resolves unbounded refs with those bounds (packages/sheets/src/formula/formula.ts:414-417), whereas the calculator expands the same reference against `sheet.getUsedBounds()` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts:90-92, sheet.ts:2604-2606). `=SUM(A:A)` therefore highlights a different extent than the cells actually summed.

per_sample.summary: `getUsedBounds` is a new *required* member of the publicly exported `Store` interface — a breaking change for any out-of-repo implementer
per_sample.evidence: packages/sheets/src/store/store.ts:80 adds `getUsedBounds(): Promise<Range | undefined>` with no default, and `Store` is re-exported from the package entry point (packages/sheets/src/index.ts:351). All three in-repo implementations were updated (memory.ts:315, readonly.ts:157, packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:614), so the breakage is only for external implementers; making it optional (with an `undefined` fallback in Sheet.getUsedBounds) would avoid it.

per_sample.summary: A whole-column total placed in the same column now self-references, because the used bounds include the formula cell itself
per_sample.evidence: `CellIndex.bounds()` (packages/sheets/src/store/cell-index.ts:128-149) counts the formula cell, so `=SUM(A:A)` written in A100 expands to `A1:A100` and `MemStore.buildDependantsMap` (packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts:333) records A100 as a dependant of itself, feeding a self-edge into `calculate`'s cycle handling (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts). I could not confirm how `calculate` reacts to a self-edge (graceful `#REF!` vs. hang); a column-total in its own column is a common layout, and no test covers it.
